newsitem.title: Indonesia: Thirteen dead in pre-poll violence in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen dead in pre-poll violence in East Timor.

text.p: At least 13 people died in a wave of election-eve violence in East Timor in a bid by government opponents to disrupt Indonesia's general elections on Thursday, police said.
Residents in the capital Dili and the second town of Baucau said they were woken by shooting and explosions late on Wednesday and early Thursday.
East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam said by telephone police shot four rebels dead in an attack on a mobile brigade or riot police post on the outskirts of Dili on Wednesday night.
"From the rebels there were four dead and four captured alive. They received gunshot wounds. Four police were injured by gunfire. No police were killed," Muharam said.
"In Baucau, there were two citizens shot dead. In Los Palos, there were seven citizens shot dead and two seriously injured," he said.
He said three people were also kidnapped in Los Palos, about 200 km (124 miles) east of the capital. "Security forces are now tracking them," he added.
Diplomatic analysts said it was the biggest upsurge in fatal violence in East Timor in recent years.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed the territory the following year as its 27th province in a move still not recognised by the United Nations.
The territory went to the polls peacefully on Thursday after police said the rebel attempt to disrupt election day failed.

"There was lots of shooting last night in Dili at around 10 p.m. (1400 GMT), but nobody seemed to immediately know what is was about. Things have returned to normal this morning with traffic moving and people voting," one Dili resident said by telephone.
Tension was high with other residents reporting an unusual amount of military air traffic.
"There was a big explosion followed by a lot of gunfire at about 2 a.m. (1800 GMT) but we are still in the dark what it was all about," a resident of Baucau, 100 km (62 miles) east of Dili, said.
The military estimates there are about 80 anti-Indonesian guerrillas operating in the rugged territory, although other sources say the number could be up to a couple of hundred.
The Indonesian armed forces keep a strong presence there.

Sources in Dili said the attack on the mobile brigade post on the outskirts of town was highly unusual and there appeared to have been some communication between the two sides before shooting took place.
One diplomat watching East Timor closely said the territory had been very tense in recent days after two police were killed in an ambush by a platoon-sized unit of rebels near Baucau on Tuesday.
A similiar sized rebel unit was involved in an ambush in Viqueque last month in which four soldiers and two government officials were killed.
"There have been a lot of leaflets circulating in East Timor that the rebels would try to disrupt the election," the source said.
Muharam said a number of polling stations in East Timor had been destroyed by opponents of Indonesia's rule.
"(The rebels) wanted to threaten the people and scare them so they did not join the election. But all the people this morning have joined the election," Muharam said.
"The polling stations that were burnt last night have been repaired by officials and the situations is normal this morning," he added.
